items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And you find that the reason Scott Fitzgerald had whatever obsession he had, I guess he was, it was important to kind of do social climbing at a certain age in his life.

ctx.x: Musically, what was the biggest difference between Basie and Ellington?

Well Ellington got to my gut you know, all those passioned, romantic, beautiful things. And I was an only child and I was home alone a lot, and you know you put the phonograph on and you just — I think it’s when certain things enter your realm. You know your pores are open when you’re developing a teenager. When you’re 17, 18, you’re very receptive. And you find that the reason Scott Fitzgerald had whatever obsession he had, I guess he was, it was important to kind of do social climbing at a certain age in his…
A little more dance oriented perhaps?
